clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive deficiency of IRAK-4 impairs signalling through most Toll-like receptors (all except TLR3) and through the whole interleukin-1 receptor family.
Susceptibility is narrow but dangerous: recurrent invasive pyogenic bacterial infection, especially Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
The hallmark is a blunted inflammatory response, so patients may lack fever and have deceptively low acute-phase markers despite invasive infection.
Resistance to most viruses, fungi, parasites and other bacteria is preserved, unlike broad immunodeficiencies.
The risk of life-threatening infection is highest in infancy and early childhood and characteristically improves with age.
Routine immunological screening such as immunoglobulins and blood counts is often normal, so a high index of suspicion is essential.
Prophylactic antibiotics, immunoglobulin replacement and vaccination against encapsulated organisms reduce the infection burden.
reference.pathophysiology: IRAK-4 is a serine/threonine kinase that acts immediately downstream of the adaptor MyD88 in Toll-like receptor signalling (all receptors except TLR3) and in interleukin-1 receptor family signalling. Biallelic loss-of-function variants abolish IRAK-4 kinase activity, preventing recruitment and activation of IRAK-1, downstream NF-kappaB and MAPK activation, and production of proinflammatory cytokines in response to Toll-like and interleukin-1 receptor stimulation. The resulting failure of early innate inflammatory responses explains susceptibility to invasive pyogenic and encapsulated bacteria and the strikingly attenuated fever and acute-phase response, while intact TLR3 and MyD88-independent pathways preserve antiviral and broader host defence. Susceptibility tends to narrow with age as adaptive immunity matures.
additionalDifferentials: Complement deficiency, particularly early and terminal components
additionalInvestigations: Functional Toll-like and interleukin-1 receptor assays showing impaired cytokine responses to agonists
Whole-blood cytokine production tests after receptor stimulation
Baseline immunoglobulins, blood counts and complement to exclude alternative diagnoses
Blood film for splenic-function markers such as Howell-Jolly bodies
Prompt cultures and microbiological sampling during febrile or invasive episodes
redFlags: Invasive pyogenic infection (bacteraemia, meningitis, deep abscess) with a paradoxically muted fever or acute-phase response
Recurrent invasive pneumococcal or staphylococcal disease in a young child
Rapid clinical deterioration despite minimal inflammatory markers
reference.prognosis: Mortality is highest in the first years of life during invasive episodes, but with prophylaxis, vaccination and prompt aggressive treatment the outlook improves markedly, and susceptibility wanes with age.
pitfalls: Relying on fever or acute-phase markers to gauge severity, since both may be misleadingly low.
Assuming that normal immunoglobulins and blood counts exclude an inborn error of immunity.
Delaying empirical antibiotics while awaiting confirmatory signs of inflammation.
Overlooking the diagnosis in an older, less symptomatic patient who has a suggestive childhood history.
references: IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
ESID clinical guidance on innate immune defects
management: Give continuous antibacterial prophylaxis, typically with penicillin, through the high-risk years of infancy and early childhood
Immunise fully against encapsulated organisms with pneumococcal, Haemophilus influenzae type b and meningococcal conjugate vaccines
Treat any febrile or suspected invasive episode promptly and aggressively with empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics, since the inflammatory response is blunted and acute-phase markers may mislead
Educate the family to seek urgent medical care for any fever given the attenuated acute-phase response
Consider immunoglobulin replacement in selected patients with recurrent infection
Maintain a low threshold for cultures and microbiological sampling during episodes
Offer genetic counselling and family testing for this autosomal recessive condition
